stories.headline: Run game, defense power Broncos in OT win against Seahawks
stories.summary: Behind two rushing touchdowns and a five-sack night, Denver holds off Seattle on "Thursday Night Football."
stories.body:
DENVER -- In a season in which the Denver Broncos' offense has struggled mightily to construct many scoring drives, let alone big plays, they used just enough small ones to grind out a 17-14 overtime victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night in Empower Field at Mile High.

In coach Sean Payton's second game since he took back playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, the Broncos put together a 16-play drive for their first touchdown of the game -- their longest drive of the season -- to go with a nine-play, 79-yard touchdown for their second one. Denver then survived without another scoring drive.

Payton has preached a need for a reduction in "calories" in the offense as well as more physicality in the run game to make life easier on quarterback Bo Nix. All while the Broncos' defense, which was without All-Pro Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga in the secondary, continued its quarterback-harassing ways. Denver had its second consecutive game with five sacks and an overtime interception from Ja'Quan McMillian.

The Broncos ran it more than they threw it in the Week 5 win against the Los Angeles Chargers and had the scale tipped squarely toward the run game most of the night against the Seahawks -- 26 runs compared to 27 pass attempts before Wil Lutz kicked the winning field goal.

The victory might not have been suitable for framing, given the Broncos didn't score after the first quarter and had to survive an 11-point fourth quarter from the Seahawks, but it was enough by the wafer-thinnest of margins.

It meant the Broncos have navigated the toughest six-game opening stretch of any team in the league, per ESPN Analytics, with wins against both teams from the NFC Championship Game last season as well as five teams that were in the postseason, culminating in a 4-2 record.

Here are the most important things to know from Thursday night for both teams:

Denver Broncos (4-2)
Trend to watch: The Broncos, from Payton on down, probably have expended more energy, spoken more words, spent more time in thought and still more aspirin in the pursuit of faster starts in games. And yet they have finished every opening drive of every game -- including Thursday night -- with either a punt or a turnover (there were five punts and one interception in the season opener). And their Week 5 win against the Chargers was the only opening drive of a game to go even more than three plays.

Stat to know: With Thursday's win, Payton's teams have now won 40 consecutive games when they had a double-digit lead at halftime. The Broncos led 14-3 at halftime. The last time a Payton team lost a game when it had a double-digit lead at halftime was Week 1 of the 2014 season when the New Orleans Saints led 20-10 at halftime and lost the game 37-34.

What to make of the QB performance: Payton obviously meant what he said when he put himself back on the headset, that there would be "more balance" between run and pass to try to dial things down for Nix. Thursday's game was a low-risk, low-reward affair as Nix didn't have a completion longer than 16 yards and never really looked settled against a Seahawks pass rush that came in with a league-best 65.5% pass rush win rate. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: at Arizona Cardinals (Oct. 25)

Seattle Seahawks (3-3)
The Seahawks' offense is officially broken. As a result, the defending champions are in serious trouble. In one of their most agonizing offensive showings since Mike Macdonald became their head coach in 2024, the Seahawks managed only 184 yards through the first three quarters, gave up five sacks of quarterback Sam Darnold and turned the ball over three more times -- including interceptions in the fourth quarter and overtime.

Adding to the inexplicability of it all is the fact the Broncos were missing their best defensive player in Surtain and another difference-maker in safety Talanoa Hufanga. It wasted a standout performance by Seattle's defense, which continues to keep the Seahawks in games despite their offensive struggles.

First-year coordinator Brian Fleury's unit entered Week 6 ranked eighth in scoring, but that was buoyed by Seattle's defense and special teams, which have been covering for the offense's flaws -- too many turnovers, Darnold's inability to play decisively, the lack of a credible run game and breakdowns in pass protection.

With the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers playing the one-win Washington Commanders at home Monday night, the Seahawks could be three games behind in the NFC West standings by the time Week 6 is over -- with one loss already to their division rival.

What to make of the QB performance: After taking five sacks Sunday in a loss to the 49ers, Darnold made it clear this week that he needs to play more decisively. That still appeared to be an issue Thursday, with the quarterback bypassing open receivers and trying unsuccessfully to extend plays. At times, though, his pass protection gave him no chance. Darnold showed his mettle by leading a touchdown and field goal drive in the fourth quarter to bookend his fourth-quarter interception. But after entering this game ranked 29th in Total QBR, he now has as many picks as touchdown passes -- seven -- in the four games since he returned from a glute injury.

Trend to watch: As good as Seattle's defense is, it can't keep teams out of the end zone in goal-to-go situations. The Seahawks' opponents have had nine of them over the first six games and have scored touchdowns on all of them -- including two by Denver on Thursday night. Not that you can fault Macdonald's unit for this one. After the Broncos' back-to-back long touchdown drives in the first half, Seattle's defense gave them nothing.

Stat to know: This was Jaxon Smith-Njigba's fourth career game with at least 10 catches and 100 receiving yards, tying Tyler Lockett for most in team history. The league's leading receiver and the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year (12 catches for 134 yards) entered Thursday having gotten 34.8% of the Seahawks' targets -- by far the largest target share of any NFL player. He had some help for a change, with Rashid Shaheed (66 yards) and Cooper Kupp (50 yards) both topping 50 receiving yards and combining for 18 targets. -- Brady Henderson

Next game: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Oct. 25)

stories.headline: MLB playoffs: Takeaways from NLCS Game 4, ALCS Game 3
stories.summary: Milwaukee swept L.A. to advance to the World Series, while Cleveland took a 2-1 ALCS lead over Tampa Bay.
stories.body:
On Day 5 of the league championship series, one team broke a series tie ... and another advanced to the World Series.

In the finale of the National League Championship Series, the Milwaukee Brewers pulled off yet another come-from-behind win to sweep the reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium and advance to their first Fall Classic since 1982.

After splitting the first two games in Tampa Bay, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays faced off at Progressive Field in the day's first game. Thanks to Petey Halpin -- and his epic bat flip -- Cleveland prevailed, taking a 2-1 American League Championship Series lead.

We have you covered with in-game action and postgame analysis from Los Angeles and Cleveland.

Key links: How final four teams were built | Playoff MVP tracker | Schedule

Jump to: TB-CLE | MIL-LAD

Milwaukee Brewers 6, Los Angeles Dodgers 4
Milwaukee wins series 4-0

It was over when ... David Hamilton blasted a home run with two outs in the top of the ninth inning, extending the Milwaukee lead to two runs -- which, for a Dodgers offense that was already down, must have felt like a finishing body blow. At the moment of contact, a collective ooooh could be heard in the lowest bowl of Dodger Stadium.

The stat that defined the game: The Dodgers went 2-for-11 with runners in scoring position, repeatedly squandering chances to tie the game in the final innings. They had a runner at second and one out in the sixth, a runner at third with one out in the seventh and a runner at third with one out in the eighth. Time and again, they could not plate the run they needed to knot the score. -- Buster Olney

Game 4 star: After a typical Brewers rally from a four-run deficit (they tied it up with no home runs), Garrett Mitchell lit up Dodgers lefty Tanner Scott for a go-ahead solo homer in the sixth. The rally typified how the Brewers play when they are at their best, and the lockdown bullpen always deserves plaudits. But it was Mitchell's blast that put Milwaukee in position to roll out its "A" bullpen with a lead to protect. -- Bradford Doolittle

More stats from the Brewers' sweep of the Dodgers
• After being swept by the Dodgers in last October's NLCS, the Brewers are the first team in MLB history to sweep the opponent that swept it in the previous postseason.

• All of the Brewers' wins this postseason have been credited to relief pitchers; since the LCS was instituted in 1969, no team has reached the World Series without a starting pitcher recording a win.

• The Brewers become the first team in MLB history with six comeback wins over its first eight games of a postseason.

• The Brewers are the fifth team in MLB history to overcome a four-plus-run deficit to clinch a best-of-seven playoff series and the first to do it to finish a sweep.

• The Game 4 win was the Brewers' fifth straight, the longest streak in franchise postseason history. (They also won four straight in 1982 and 2018.)

• The Dodgers are the fifth reigning World Series champions to be swept in a best-of-seven series (first since 1990 Athletics vs. Reds in the World Series). The last reigning WS champions that were swept in any series were the 2005 Red Sox (ALDS vs. White Sox) and the only back-to-back defending champions that were swept in a playoff series were the 1975 Athletics (ALCS vs. Red Sox) and 1963 Yankees (World Series vs. Dodgers).

• This was the Dodgers' seventh straight game with fewer than five runs scored, their longest streak since a seven-game streak in June 2018 (regular season and postseason).

Highlights from Milwaukee's win
Brewers complete the sweep, punch their ticket to the World Series

Milwaukee adds an insurance run in the 9th

Dodgers continue to struggle with runners in scoring position

Brewers take lead off of Mitchell's solo homer

A bases-loaded walk from Vesia ties the game

Bauers' 2-run double makes it 4-2

Ohtani breaks slump with 3-run blast to give L.A. 4-run lead

Pages gets Dodgers on the board first

Game 4 kicks off with wild play

Cleveland Guardians 3, Tampa Bay Rays 2
Cleveland leads series 2-1

It was over when ... Petey Halpin cranked a 96 mph sinker down the middle from Griffin Jax in the fifth inning. The ball landed deep into the right-field seats, 385 feet away, for a go-ahead two-run home run. Halpin flipped his bat nearly that high, too, and Cleveland didn't look back.

Game 3 star: Halpin, who began the season in Triple-A, had four big league home runs -- all during the regular season -- in 213 career plate appearances before Thursday. The center fielder's first postseason homer was the difference Thursday.

The stat that defined the game: The Rays' 13 strikeouts against Guardians pitching. The Rays posted the lowest strikeout rate in the majors this season at 18.8%. They struck out more than 12 times once, when they compiled 14 strikeouts against the Milwaukee Brewers back on March 30 in their fourth game of the season. Rays star Junior Caminero went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts -- matching a career high from 2025. So Thursday was an extreme outlier. Guardians starter Gavin Williams, the American League's strikeout leader this season, had nine strikeouts in five innings before four relievers combined for the remaining four punchouts. Tampa Bay will have to put the ball in play more to come back and win this series.

What it means for the rest of the series: With rain in the forecast Friday, there's a chance this series won't play Game 4 until Saturday. If so, the clubs would play Game 5 on Sunday, which would take away their travel day before a potential Game 6 in Tampa Bay on Monday. For now, Game 4 is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET on Friday. -- Jorge Castillo

Highlights from Cleveland's win

Halpin's homer, um, flips lead back to Guardians

Simpson silences Cleveland crowd with two-run triple

Gavin gettin' it done early

Guardians score first on Lowe's double

A series-defining day?

stories.headline: Utah Mammoth beat the Oilers 4-2 as Clayton Keller scores twice
stories.summary: — Clayton Keller scored a pair of goals and the Utah Mammoth snapped Edmonton's five-game win streak with a 4-2 victory over the Oilers on Thursday night.
stories.body:
EDMONTON, Alberta -- — Clayton Keller scored a pair of goals and the Utah Mammoth snapped Edmonton's five-game win streak with a 4-2 victory over the Oilers on Thursday night.


Barrett Hayton and Logan Cooley also scored for the Mammoth, who have won three straight. Karel Vejmelka stopped 22 shots.


Leon Draisaitl and Shakir Mukhamadullin scored for the Oilers, who were missing five starting forwards and a defenseman. Devon Levi made 20 saves for Edmonton.


Just 23 seconds after Draisaitl got Edmonton on the board at 13:54 of the second period to pull the Oilers within 2-1, Vincent Trocheck sent he puck in front to a hard-charging Cooley, who directed in his first of the season to restore Utah’s two-goal lead.


Connor McDavid picked up an assist to extend his season-starting points streak to seven games. He now has four goals and 14 assists for a league-leading 18 points, his best start to a season.


Utah should be pleased that it matched the offer sheet tendered by the New Jersey Devils for Hayton in the offseason. Hayton scored his first of the season and extended his points streak to five games.


Edmonton came into the contest with a 5-0-1 record against the Mammoth while outscoring them 31-16. Edmonton was also 3-0-0 all-time at home against Utah, outscoring the Mammoth 17-5.


Up next
Mammoth: Host the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.


Oilers: At the Utah Mammoth on Saturday.

stories.body:
Eberechi Eze's next goal celebration has been determined by YouTuber IShowSpeed after the Arsenal forward was beaten by the influencer in an EA Sports FC battle.

The best-of-three showdown was ultimately decided in favour of Speed, the 21-year-old streamer who has amassed 61.7 million subscribers on YouTube.

As a result, Eze will have to do a celebration of Speed's choosing -- a combination of Cristiano Ronaldo's trademark "siuuu" ritual and the streamer's signature bark, as well as a badge tap and a knee lift.

The Arsenal attacker chose Paris Saint-Germain for the opening match, with Speed questioning his decision not to choose Arsenal.

"I ride or die for my team, but on FIFA?" Eze replied. "I'm not sure about that."

Eze did play with his own team in the second game, before he lost to Speed who -- playing as Bayern Munich -- scored a dramatic late winner in the decider through ex-Tottenham man Harry Kane.

Speed initially suggested his own cross-arms celebration followed by twerking, a combination Eze rejected after laughing and saying: "I won't lie to you, that bounce thing is berserk."

He revealed he did not know how to backflip, which was option two, so the pair settled on the Ronaldo-inspired celebration.

stories.headline: U.S. prodigy Cavan Sullivan sets MLS record, laments 'terrible' performance
stories.summary: U.S. teen prodigy Cavan Sullivan made more history on Wednesday, but the Philadelphia Union midfielder insisted he was less than happy with his performance.
stories.body:
United States teen prodigy Cavan Sullivan made more history on Wednesday night, but the Philadelphia Union midfielder insisted he was less than happy with his performance.

Sullivan, who turned 17 last month, picked up his 14th assist of the season to set up Bruno Damiani's game winner in the Union's 3-1 victory at the Chicago Fire FC.

- Miami, Messi clinch playoffs with win over NYCFC

- St. Louis City unbeaten run reaches record 21 after draw with Whitecaps

Together with his seven goals, Sullivan now has 21 goal contributions in his breakout year, the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season.

The 14 assists put him second in MLS, level with Inter Miami's Lionel Messi and behind only Son Heung-Min of LAFC (15). Sullivan has a goal contribution in 10 straight MLS games, registering 16 in that span.

Sullivan had already broken the mark for most goal contributions in an MLS season for a player under 17, besting the mark set by former U.S. soccer phenom, Freddy Adu.

Yet he was in a less than celebratory mood after his latest achievement.

"I played sort of terrible tonight, so I'm not really focused on any records or stats like that, to be honest," Sullivan said.

"I'm happy with the win, but I've sort of got to look in the mirror and watch some film and see what I have to do better. I'm not really happy with my personal performance, but, like I said, great win."

Union interim coach Ryan Richter, though, was more positive about his young star.

"It seems like every week something else is popping up for him," Richter said.

"I'm so happy for him, and a big emphasis for him is to continue to be decisive in games, and when he's chipping in with goals and assists, the way that he has over this last stretch, he's making the difference."

Sullivan's form has carried Philadelphia to eight straight wins and a club-record 14-match unbeaten streak to move up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference with five games of the regular season remaining.

Sullivan, who ESPN has reported has an agreement to join Manchester City when he turns 18, recently made history with the U.S. men's national team.

He became the youngest player to start a game for the USMNT since Adu 20 years earlier when he made his debut still aged 16 last month. He followed that up by becoming the youngest scorer ever for the USMNT with a stunning long-range goal in a victory over Mexico.

stories.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
stories.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

An ethnic Russian, but Donetsk-born and bred, Akhmetov's huge wealth from mining and energy bankrolled the club's rise to prominence prewar -- lest we forget, the likes of Willian and Fernandinho, Henrikh Mkiytaryan and Douglas Costa are all Shakhtar alums -- and keeps it alive and very much kicking today. Forbes estimates his wealth at nearly $8 billion and like most folks of that ilk, Akhmetov could easily have made different choices, decamping abroad. When the war broke out, he chose to stay, and that was not something to take for granted, given that he had previously clashed with Zelenskyy and, in the 2000s, served in parliament in the party of former pro-Russian Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych, whom he also backed financially.

Akhmetov broke with Yanukovych in 2014 and while his pro-Ukrainian words today are loud, his actions -- from staying in the country to tirelessly campaigning to his efforts with Shakhtar -- speak even louder.

"He can't leave Ukraine, not after seeing what he has seen," Srna says of Akhmetov. "It's impossible. He's devoted himself to this, helping the economy, helping the people. All while sleeping each night under bombs."

Many Ukrainians have no choice, which makes the actions of those who could be elsewhere all the more remarkable. It takes an unconventional type of person.

Most of Shakhtar's players are Brazilian -- lured by money, sure, but also the opportunity to showcase their talent. The coach, former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona standout Arda Turan, is Turkish. Even if you don't remember what he was like as a player, watching him prowl the technical area during the AEK game, fists clenched and eyes wild, you come to understand how this is the same guy who once got into an altercation with a pop star in an Istanbul hospital, a brawl that ended in him firing a gun into the floor.

Srna himself is Croatian, but has been at the club -- first as a player then as sporting director -- for 23 years. He too could have left umpteen times and, in fact, he says he even turned down the chance to take over Barcelona's recruitment a decade ago.

"Ukraine and Shakhtar are in my blood," he says. "If I leave now, I couldn't live with myself."

In some ways, Srna has been here before. He was eight years old when civil war broke out in the former Yugoslavia in March 1991. The conflict that would rage for 4½ years, ripped apart communities along ethnic lines. Neighbors took up arms against neighbors. His own father woke up every day supplying baked goods for the military. If you've seen the ESPN 30 for 30 documentary "Once Brothers" about the relationship between Drazen Petrovic and Vlade Divac, well ... he lived it. Twice. Maybe that's why he soldiers on, numb to what he is experiencing.

"I have this feeling inside myself," he says. "It's a feeling I felt before [as a child experiencing war in Croatia]. But when you feel that pain and it comes back to you again, well, you're not going to have the same pain twice. I know this pain. I know this feeling ..."

Srna trails off as he searches for the right words of history -- the worst parts -- repeating itself with him in the middle of it. But then he flickers back with righteous anger.

"This is unbelievable, I can't explain it," he says. "Four-and-a-half years [this war has continued]. Bombing each other, destroying everything ... for what? For f---ing what? People die, families are destroyed, children are traumatized and grow up with psychological problems ..."

On this Wednesday night, even as Shakhtar emerge as 3-1 victors over AEK, you're reminded once again of the difficulties. The team were up at 6 a.m. on Thursday to catch a 10 o'clock flight on a plane they chartered from a budget airline taking them back to Rzeszow in Poland. They'll then board a bus back across the border into Ukraine, arriving -- best-case scenario -- at 9 p.m. local time. All this not knowing whether they'll have power and heat when they arrive, or whether they'll be making regular trips into the air raid shelter.

You want to end on a note of hope. Srna does his best to offer it, but he clearly isn't going to lie to you or to himself.

"We [Croatians] have more or less an OK relationship now with Serbia," he says. "Time [30 years have passed] is helping, generations change, it's different people. We take a step back and understand what was good, what was not good. We can't say all Serbian people are bad ... But in this moment, it's not possible to be friends with a Russian person. In time, maybe a few years, maybe many years, I don't know ... right now though, it's impossible."

Certainly more impossible than a club without a home in a country at war defying logic and competing in the Champions League against the likes of Real Madrid, who visit Stamford Bridge on Jan. 27.

One of the side effects of war is the normalization of the horrific and the absurd. Shakhtar's plight has, by necessity, normalized the absurd, in an effort to stave off the horrific.

stories.headline: UFC champ Alexander Volkanovski proposes 'send-off' superbout vs. Justin Gaethje
stories.summary: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski is calling for a "send-off" superfight against lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.
stories.body:
UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski has proposed a "send-off" superfight between himself and lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Volkanovski (28-4) is scheduled to defend his 145-pound title against Movsar Evloev (20-0) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Arguably the greatest featherweight of all time, Volkanovski has acknowledged he is approaching the end of his career at 38 years old. Gaethje, 37, has acknowledged the same since he claimed the UFC's 155-pound title for the first time in June.

With both champions seemingly near the end of their time in the Octagon, Volkanovski has suggested a winner-take-all scenario in 2027.

"Imagine that, do it as a send-off," Volkanovski told the "Who Da Fook Are These Guys?" podcast. "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

Volkanovski, of Australia, has already tried to capture the lightweight title. He famously challenged then-lightweight champion Islam Makhachev twice in a 10-month span in 2023. He suffered a razor-close decision loss to Makhachev in their first meeting in February then lost by first-round knockout in an October rematch that was scheduled on short notice.

Gaethje (28-5) has not even guaranteed whether he will fight again or retire off his historic win at the White House in June, but he has stated that he believes his next challenger would be lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski appears to be throwing his name into the mix in the hope of changing those plans.

"He's said, 'What's the point of doing rematches,'" Volkanovski said. "Let's do a superfight then [retire] straight away after, let the divisions sort themselves out. The UFC would be happy for that. Let's make it happen."

stories.headline: Why is Max Verstappen racing in GT World Challenge? Schedule, how to watch latest non-F1 event
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest motorsport challenge.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest racing challenge.

There is little time for rest for the Dutchman, who heads to Portimão to compete in the latest GT World Challenge event, sandwiched between two F1 triple-headers.

The one-off event will also feature some of the best drivers in the world, including World Endurance Championship title winner Nicki Thiim, nine-time MotoGP world champion Valentino Rossi, who competes for BMW in the World Endurance Championship, and Ferrari development driver Arthur Leclerc.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

Why is Verstappen racing this weekend?

Verstappen has been one of the biggest critics around F1's controversial new regulations, calling them "anti-racing."

Things are, however, on the up after he took his first victory this season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, before following it up with a dominant win in Singapore, as Red Bull continue to thrive with its upgraded package.

Despite finding success in F1, the simple reason why he's back to GT racing this weekend is due to some of Verstappen Racing's usual drivers not being available to compete. Dani Juncadella and Jules Gounon have a World Endurance Championship calendar clash with the Portuguese round on Oct. 18.

Verstappen decided to step in and will be racing alongside Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham.

"I know that two of my drivers won't be part of the line-up, so two other drivers need to step in and I'm looking forward to it," Verstappen said.

"It's going to be a busy seven weeks, but we'll do it and I enjoy it anyway. So, yeah. Let's see what we can do there."

It's set to be a busy weekend with the GT2 European Series, GT4 European Series and McLaren Trophy Europe all set to crown their champions.

The 29-year-old will be back in his Red Bull a week later in Texas for F1's United States Grand Prix, where he will target a third win in a row.

GT World Challenge schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, October 15

Official Paid Test Session 1: 11.50 a.m.

Bronze test: 5.40 p.m.

Friday, October 16

Free Practice 1: 8.45 a.m.

Qualifying: 5.55 p.m. - 7.05 p.m.

Saturday, October 17

Race: 5 p.m. - 8 p.m.

How to watch

The GT World Challenge will be streamed on the official GT World YouTube Channel or via the GT World Challenge Europe website.

Portimão Circuit

Built in the Algarve region in southern Portugal, the circuit is a mix of fast and slow corners which features some extreme elevation changes.

There are overtaking opportunities, but the 4.653km track is considered challenging with its 16 corners.

It's so popular that it's returning to the F1 calendar in 2027 and 2028. The race next year will take the place of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

Weather forecast

The weather forecast for the race in Portimão is set to be sunny with a gentle breeze, with highs of 27°C on Thursday through to race day on Saturday.

Verstappen's other racing ventures

During his debut GT3 race in the Nürburgring Endurance Series in September last year he landed a stunning victory in a Ferrari 296 entered by Emil Frey Racing.

In March, he drove a Mercedes-AMG GT3 through Verstappen Racing in the preliminary NLS2 race which is a four-hour endurance race. He won the race but was later disqualified over a tyre error.

A few months later he competed in one of motor racing's toughest endurance tests -- the iconic Nürburgring 24-hour race under Verstappen Racing driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3 Evo.

He came close to ticking a dream off his list, but his car suffered a driveshaft issue with three hours of the race remaining.

Verstappen more recently took part in a more lighthearted challenge where he took on 100 creators and sports personalities in go-karts starting from the back of the grid. Nobody was sure how the race would unravel at the custom-built track at Silverstone, but he ended up passing every single driver to lead the race after 35 minutes.

stories.headline: AFL trade and free agency grades - Every club's report card from the 2026 transfer period
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is over. Some teams improved, some stagnated, and others, well, got worse. Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is complete. Some teams improved, some have stagnated, and others, well, seemed to have gotten worse.

READ: Every player move from the 2026 off-season

Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks:

Adelaide
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Jordon Butts, Luke Pedlar

2026 draft selections: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92

I'm not sure what the Crows' gameplan was this trade and free agency period, but it's fair to say the club sat on its hands and did next to nothing. Losing key defender Jordon Butts to the Bulldogs obviously weakens them, while just one draft selection inside the top 30 is unlikely to provide much immediate support. Adelaide's list profile remains fine, and maybe they will surprise us all in 2027, but you just get the sense so many other clubs have passed them by over the last two weeks.

Grade: F

Brisbane
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Lachie Neale, Sam Marshall, Will McLachlan, Keidean Coleman

2026 draft selections: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97

The Lions were the biggest winners of last year's off-season (and season!), but this year was a different story. All year it seemed a formality they would lose the services of dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale, who ultimately signed with Collingwood as a free agent. They also waved goodbye to Keidean Coleman and Sam Marshall, two players who had struggled to crack the best 23 of late. No picks inside the top 20 would be concerning for 17 other clubs, but the Lions still have so much young talent at their disposal and are primed to challenge again in 2027.

Grade: C-

Carlton
Incoming: Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield

Outgoing: Hudson O'Keeffe, Flynn Riley

2026 draft selections: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90

The Blues addressed two areas of weakness this off-season. The addition of free agent Joel Amartey provides spearhead Harry McKay with a stable forward line partner, while the Lachie Whitfield signing offers run, experience, and a kick-first option off halfback, the perfect piece to fit into Josh Fraser's system. Carlton really didn't give up much to land Whitfield, either. And barring Essendon taking a stab at talented father-son prospect Cody Walker with pick No. 1, the club has also ensured it has enough draft capital to match any bids that will come for him.

Grade: A

Collingwood
Incoming: Lachie Neale, Jesse Hogan, Flynn Riley

Outgoing: Scott Pendlebury

2026 draft selections: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88

The Magpies had been crying out for a true inside midfielder, and they landed arguably the best in the competition in Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow Medal winner is an elite ball winner and clearance player, and should perfectly complement superstar Nick Daicos. Collingwood also signed Jesse Hogan, a man that won the Coleman Medal just two years ago, and gave up virtually nothing for him. The loss of champion Scott Pendlebury obviously stings, but you have to feel this club is in a stronger position now than it was two weeks ago.

Grade: A

Essendon
Incoming: Jack Bowes, Keidean Coleman

Outgoing: Zach Merrett, Jordan Ridley

2026 draft selections: 1, 17, 25, 80

Former skipper Zach Merrett finally got his wish of a fresh start at the Hawks, while fellow experienced player Jordan Ridley also departs the club for the Cats. The additions of Jack Bowes and Keidean Coleman are fine, but are either going to be difference makers in a side that's been languishing at the bottom of the ladder for several years? I'm not so sure. The only saving grace for the Bombers is that they hold pick No. 1. They simply have to make the most of that selection.

Grade: D

Fremantle
Incoming: Dom Bedendo

Outgoing: Nathan O'Driscoll

2026 draft selections: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96

The Dockers were incredibly quiet during the trade and free agency window, but that's not exactly a bad thing. Remember, if not for Will Ashcroft and Logan Morris, Fremantle win the 2026 premiership. There was absolutely no reason for the Dockers to panic and overpay for someone after their Grand Final heartbreak, instead, this club, with its plethora of youth and talent, should feel as if it can contend for years to come. Trust the process and go again in 2027.

Grade: C

Geelong
Incoming: Toby Greene, Jordan Ridley, Rowan Marshall

Outgoing: Jack Bowes

2026 draft selections: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93

Every year the Cats just find a way to bring big names through the door, and 2026 was no exception. Rowan Marshall was tipped to join 12 months ago and finally makes the move from St Kilda to bolster the club's ruck stocks. Toby Greene adds class, experience, and unrivalled goal-kicking nous to the forward line. Jordan Ridley is a stable and still wildly underrated defensive asset. The best part? To land this trio the club only had to give up midfield depth piece Jack Bowes, and some draft capital. They won't be much of a feature at the upcoming draft, but they don't have to be. These Cats are in win-now mode.

Grade: A

Gold Coast Suns
Incoming: Scott Pendlebury, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler

Outgoing: Ben King

2026 draft selections: 8, 85

Scott Pendlebury might be a champion of the game, but there's no denying the Suns just got worse. The addition of 38-year-old Pendlebury doesn't outweigh the seismic loss of spearhead Ben King, a man who has booted 230 goals over the last four seasons. How do they replace him? Perhaps it's the incoming Aidan Schubert, but he's years away from having a real impact. Making matters worse, it seems Brownlow medallist Matt Rowell is likely to request a trade back to Victoria at the end of next season. This club is in a real precarious spot right now. A penny for Christian Petracca's thoughts...

Grade: C-

GWS Giants
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield

2026 draft selections: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86

Just two years ago Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, and Lachie Whitfield were probably four of the Giants' most important players. None of them remain at the club after an action-packed trade and free agency window, with GWS instead opting to clear out and trust the youth underneath. It's a move that will either make the Giants look like geniuses or total fools, but even those who are incredibly bullish about the approach would concede there is likely to be some pain on the immediate horizon.

Grade: D

Hawthorn
Incoming: Zach Merrett, Ben King, Josh Goater

Outgoing: Finn Maginness, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler, Bodie Ryan

2026 draft selections: 29, 37, 71, 94

The Hawks should probably be the 2027 flag favourites after a whirlwind two weeks that's seen them finally land former Essendon skipper Zach Merrett, as well as Ben King. Merrett adds depth, experience, and A-grade ball use to Hawthorn's midfield group, while King provides a focal point in attack, taking the burden off the ageing Jack Gunston. Sure, Hawthorn gave up some depth, but their best 23 has improved out of sight and they still have draft collateral over the next few years to ensure talent keeps coming through the door.

Grade: A+

Melbourne
Incoming: Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, Bodie Ryan

Outgoing: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

2026 draft selections: 4, 14, 48, 52

Just about everyone panicked when the Demons farewelled premiership heroes Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver last year, and look how that turned out. This club seems to have a plan for the future and it isn't prepared to compromise on what it wants. Melbourne has nailed its draft picks in recent times and with selections four and 14 this year, you'd expect two more highly talented prospects to join the ranks. Who knows if Zane Duursma will work out, but they've landed him for a fraction of what the Kangaroos gave up at the draft three years ago. It's a low risk punt worth taking.

Grade: C

North Melbourne
Incoming: Nick Blakey

Outgoing: Zane Duursma, Josh Goater

2026 draft selections: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84

Credit to the Kangaroos, they finally landed a big name. The only problem is I'm not sure Nick Blakey is the superstar many are claiming. There's no doubt Blakey will add drive and dash off halfback, but is he the player you look to in the closing stages of a tight game? North also gave up a truckload of future draft capital to get him through the door which will hurt them in the coming years. And then there's the Zane Duursma fiasco. Losing a player the club invested pick No. 4 in just three years ago is an unmitigated disaster. With no selections inside the top 30 this year, it will be a rare draft without the Roos being a major player.

Grade: C+

Port Adelaide
Incoming: Luke Pedlar

Outgoing: Zak Butters

2026 draft selections: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65

You're never going to feel great when a player of Zak Butters' class and calibre walks out the door, but the silver lining for Port Adelaide is that Dougie Cochrane should be set to walk back in. The academy talent is the consensus best player in the upcoming draft and the Power are in a position to match any bids on their man. Expect Port to be heavily involved in the draft over the next couple of years as they look to rebuild around the likes of Cochrane, Connor Rozee, and Jason Horne-Francis.

Grade: B

Richmond
Incoming: Kieren Briggs, Nathan O'Driscoll

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 2, 5, 44, 81

The Tigers found Toby Nankervis' successor in Kieren Briggs, who crosses from the Giants as a free agent. That's a nice win. Nathan O'Driscoll was unable to find a place in Fremantle's best team of late but should receive far more opportunity in the black and yellow jumper in 2027. Richmond has two more picks inside the top five, though they are likely to be shuffled down a few spots with bid matching on Dougie Cochrane and Cody Walker, and they simply must nail them. Even still, this side will remain incredibly young in 2027.

Grade: C

St Kilda
Incoming: Sam Marshall

Outgoing: Rowan Marshall

2026 draft selections: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87

The Saints went all-in last year, signing Tom De Koning, Jack Silvagni, Liam Ryan, and Sam Flanders. They weren't nearly as busy this off-season, and few expected them to be. Long-time ruck Rowan Marshall departs the club for the Cats, while Sam Marshall joins and should bolster their midfield stocks. Outside of that, St Kilda will be hoping to cash in with their two first round draft selections. If not, it could spell the end of Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera's tenure. This team wouldn't want to be starting 2027 slowly...

Grade: C

Sydney Swans
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Joel Amartey, Nick Blakey

2026 draft selections: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95

Two best 23 players departed the Swans this past fortnight with halfback Nick Blakey being traded to the Kangaroos and key forward Joel Amartey signing with the Blues as a free agent. Don't forget, Callum Mills is unlikely to suit up for the entire year after suffering an ACL injury during this year's finals campaign. That's three best 23 players to replace! Who knows what's happening with Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner? Swans fans will be praying for a hit with pick No. 6 at the upcoming draft to soften the blow.

Grade: C-

West Coast Eagles
Incoming: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82

It's clear the Eagles don't want to take the same approach as the Tigers and rely solely on the kids. Instead, they're continuing to add experienced pieces around their young talent in an effort to ease the rebuild and avoid a nosedive in morale. Jack Viney and Trent Rivers add premiership experience to the club and they haven't had to give up too much to get them. West Coast will feature prominently at November's draft with pick No. 3, 23, as well as a compensation pick in the likely scenario that the club's first selection is pushed back by a bid.

Grade: C+

Western Bulldogs
Incoming: Jordon Butts, Finn Maginness, Hudson O'Keeffe, Zak Butters

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91

The Bulldogs now possess the most dynamic midfield trio in the game with Zak Butters joining skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in the red, white, and blue. It's a marquee signing for Luke Beveridge's team that simply has to put them into premiership contention. Jordon Butts also joins the club and will bolster what's traditionally been a weaker defensive unit. Don't forget about key forward star Sam Darcy, who will return from a season-ending ACL injury.

Grade: A+

stories.headline: 'All love': All Blacks inspiring NZ's Rugby League World Cup tilt
stories.summary: Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.
stories.body:
Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.

Five days after the All Blacks crushed the Wallabies 50-19 to clinch the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year, the Kiwis and Kangaroos clash in a trans-Tasman blockbuster in Sydney on Thursday night to kick off the global showpiece.

Eight ABs, including superstar winger Will Jordan and playmaker Cam Roigard, cast aside the cross-code rivalry to drop into New Zealand's captain's run on Wednesday and throw their support behind Jones's side.

"It's just all love and supporting each other and hopefully we can go watch their game on Saturday too, so it's pretty special," New Zealand captain James Fisher-Harris said.

"How dominant and how they go about their business and represent New Zealand, there's a lot of things that they do that we look up to so yeah, it's pretty cool."

Leading what he believes is "potentially" the best Kiwi forward pack ever, Fisher-Harris says "the plan" is to lift the World Cup and, like the Warriors, continue to inspire a whole new generation of rugby league players back in their homeland just like the 2008 winners did.

"When they won in 2008, I was watching Blairy (Adam Blair) and that, (Nathan) Cayless and obviously Benji (Marshall), so that made me want to go down this path," the enforcer said.

"So hopefully we can do something like that. When you are successful like that, it gets you motivated and you want to play for a certain team or a certain code.

"So that's the plan anyways, to be successful in this World Cup."

Behind the monster pack will be Kayln Ponga for the first time after the talismanic fullback, at 28, opted to represent his parents' homeland.

"He's playing pretty good right about now," Fisher-Harris said of Ponga, who led Newcastle on their magical run from seventh to a 19-18 grand final loss to the Sydney Roosters.

"But it's not just his playing ability, it's his leadership and he's been in the game for a while now.

"He's won a few things but it looks like he's pretty keen to get in that black and white jersey."

Coach Stacey Jones also believes Australia's loss is very much New Zealand's gain.

"For the Knights this year and particularly the back end of the season, he carried them to a grand final," Jones said.

"Obviously had a lot of support around him, but he's got a lot of confidence in his game at the moment and we're just lucky that we've got him on our side."

stories.headline: Broncos beat the Seahawks 17-14 in OT on Ja'Quan McMillian's pick, Wil Lutz's 53-yarder
stories.summary: — Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold's pass in overtime and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal that gave the Denver Broncos a 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold's pass in overtime and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal that gave the Denver Broncos a 17-14 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night.


The Broncos emerged from a tough six-week season-opening stretch with a 4-2 record despite an injury-riddled roster and a shaky offense, and the Seahawks (3-3) lost for the second time in five days. They also matched their loss total from last season, when they won their second Super Bowl title.


McMillian intercepted a pass intended for Rashid Shaheed at the Denver 43, the second pick of the night by Darnold, who completed 27 of 51 passes for 278 yards without a touchdown.


Those stats were better than Bo Nix's. He threw for just 107 yards on 17-of-27 passing after throwing for 123 last week in a win over the Chargers.


Jason Myers' 34-yard field goal tied it at 14-all with 3 seconds left in regulation and capped an 11-0 Seattle run over the final 5 1/2 minutes. The Seahawks started their game-tying drive at midfield after a 31-yard punt return by Shaheed following a sixth three-and-out by the Broncos.


“No moral victories in the league,” Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. “It’s a bottom-line business, production business. But I’m proud of our effort. I’m proud of the resolve of the team. I’m proud of our connectedness of our team.


“However, there’s things that we need to get better at quickly, and we know those things; they’re within our control, and that’s what we do. We find solutions, and we get things figured out, we move forward, and we evolve.”


Denver appeared to have victory in hand when Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Darnold's pass at the Denver 30 with 1:25 left in regulation, but the Broncos burned just 15 seconds of clock before punting.


After scoring just three points on their first eight drives, the Seahawks put together an 11-play, 67-yard masterpiece that ended with running back George Holani scoring from a yard out. Darnold’s 2-point pass to Shaheed pulled Seattle within 14-11 with 5:41 left.


Nix led the Broncos on two long first-half scoring drives, and Denver's depleted defense sacked Darnold five times and hit him 17 times.


“Defensively, we were magnificent,” said Broncos coach Sean Payton, who acknowledged, “I'm a little bit of a realist to know that 4-2 could easily be 2-4.”


Denver’s all-or-nothing offense produced two long drives to go with two three-and-outs before running out the clock on the first half with a 14-3 lead.


J.K. Dobbins’ 4-yard touchdown run capped a 16-play, 74-yard drive that chewed up nearly nine minutes and put Denver ahead 7-3. Running back R.J. Harvey took a direct snap and scored from a yard out on Denver’s next drive.


The Broncos sacked Darnold on back-to-back plays to thwart Seattle’s opening drive, but Denver went three-and-out on its own opening drive for the fourth time this season and the Seahawks capitalized on their good field position to take a 3-0 lead on Myers’ 55-yard field goal. He missed from 47 yards in the third quarter.


The Broncos have recorded multiple sacks in 20 consecutive home games. That’s the longest such streak in team history and the longest current streak in the NFL.


The Seahawks’ most promising first-half drive ended at the Denver 34 when Nik Bonitto punched the ball from Shaheed’s grasp and inside linebacker Justin Strnad recovered.


True to form
The Seahawks franchise fell to 19-30-1 in overtime and the Broncos improved to 33-23-2. That's second-best in the NFL.


“It was a good win,” Payton said, “but we've got a lot of work to do.”


Injuries
Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo left late in the first half with an apparent right shoulder injury sustained while diving for a fumbled ball.


The Broncos were without star CB Patrick Surtain II and starting safety Talanoa Hufanga, both out with ankle injuries. RB Tyler Badie injured a thumb in the second quarter.


Up next
Seahawks: Host the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 25.


Broncos: Host the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25.

stories.headline: Biggest offseason questions for teams eliminated from MLB playoffs
stories.summary: Here's how the winter looks in Los Angeles after the two-time defending champs were blown away by the Brewers.
stories.body:
There will be no three-peat for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The two-time defending World Series champions were swept -- yes, swept -- by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, ending their attempt to make history and eliminating them from the 2026 MLB playoffs.

What's next in Los Angeles -- and in all of the other towns that won't be celebrating a World Series parade this fall? For every eliminated contender this October, ESPN MLB experts Jorge Castillo, Bradford Doolittle, Alden Gonzalez, Jesse Rogers and David Schoenfield list its key free agents and biggest offseason questions and also make their predictions for the long, cold winter ahead.

Teams eliminated in championship series

Los Angeles Dodgers
Eliminated by: Milwaukee Brewers

Key free agents: LHP Tarik Skubal, UT Enrique Hernandez, INF Miguel Rojas, RHP Blake Treinen, RHP Evan Phillips, LHP Alex Vesia, RHP Brusdar Graterol

Biggest offseason priority: If you look at the list above, you'll see a lot of relievers. Is it a major need? No. The Dodgers still have Tanner Scott and Edwin Diaz locked up to big contracts, and Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein and Jack Dreyer ready to assume bigger roles. But it's the biggest need on a roster where the lineup and the rotation are already packed with stars and depth. Vesia in particular has been a key cog in the bullpen for many years. The Dodgers will certainly be interested in bringing him back.

The bullpen work will be relatively straightforward. The offense might not be. The Dodgers have their entire starting lineup coming back. But it also formed the oldest position-player group in baseball this season, and it struggled mightily to score runs in October. The Dodgers have always been conscious of incorporating youth whenever possible, and this October might make them more aggressive in folding in players such as Josue De Paula, Alex Freeland and Dalton Rushing.

How will they manage Shohei Ohtani? The Dodgers will probably spend a lot of time rehashing how these past four months played out with Ohtani and what they could have done differently so that his body wasn't so clearly compromised in October. The big question will be whether Ohtani will continue to pitch. Assuming he does, what exactly will that look like in his age-32 season, coming off a year in which pain in his left knee and right bicep kept him away from the rotation after early July? The Dodgers and Ohtani will have to come to an understanding. And they're going to have to communicate better.

Will a salary cap come for them? The league says its economic proposal is geared toward parity, the players counter that it's all about increasing franchise values, but if you really break it down, it's about stopping the Dodgers. If a salary cap comes to Major League Baseball, no team will be more impacted than the Dodgers, who have eight -- yes, eight -- nine-figure contracts on their payroll. And even if there isn't a cap, it's safe to say that the penalties for spending as lavishly as the Dodgers have will only become more onerous.

Offseason prediction: The Dodgers won't sign Skubal to a mega extension ... before Dec. 1. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, will probably want to get something done with his client before the lockout, but it would be really difficult for the Dodgers to justify signing Skubal to a massive deal before knowing what MLB's economic model will look like. If there is a cap-and-floor system in the next collective bargaining agreement, there will be some sort of phase-in period. But it will undoubtedly impact the Dodgers in the near future. It would be a major risk to sign Skubal before knowing what they're signing up for. -- Gonzalez

Teams eliminated in division series

Chicago White Sox
Eliminated by: Cleveland Guardians

Key free agents: LHP Sean Newcomb, OF Randal Grichuk

Biggest offseason priority: The White Sox established a nice foundation with their position players in 2026, especially in the infield, where Miguel Vargas (3B), Colson Montgomery (SS) and Munetaka Murakami (1B) each hit 30-plus home runs. And with top prospects Caleb Bonemer and No. 1 pick Roch Cholowsky on his way -- plus breakout seasons from Chase Meidroth and Sam Antonacci -- the team is more than set in that area. Where it needs work is in its starting rotation.

Sean Burke and Davis Martin led the way to the playoffs this year, but neither is a true ace. Additionally, the White Sox had the fewest innings from starting pitchers of any playoff team. They might need a little bit of a more traditional path on the mound if they want to return to October next year. Openers and multi-inning stints from relief pitchers can take you only so far -- as evidenced by the team's exit this postseason. The team can work Hagen Smith and Noah Schultz into the rotation, while Burke and Martin aren't going anywhere unless one is traded. Figuring out their five-man rotation will be the priority this winter.

What will happen with Luis Castillo in 2027? Owed $21 million for next season, Castillo was a summer trade who did not work out this year. Will the team give him another opportunity in the rotation come spring training or is he destined for the bullpen? Chicago isn't likely to let him go before next year, but if things don't turn around for the veteran once the season starts, he'll be a DFA candidate.

Offseason prediction: The White Sox will engage Murakami in discussions for a longer-term deal after his current one expires after 2027. It might not be the massive payday he was in line for when he shot out of the gate this year, but it still should end up being the largest contract earned in White Sox history. That's if both sides can come to an agreement. Whenever a player is within a year of free agency, there's always a chance he tests the market -- but in this case, there seems to be a genuine desire to complete a deal. -- Rogers

New York Yankees
Eliminated by: Tampa Bay Rays

Key free agents: RHP David Bednar, 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr., CF Trent Grisham, RHP Paul Blackburn, 1B Paul Goldschmidt

Biggest offseason priority: Restocking the relief corps. Bednar was a rock at the back end of the bullpen in 2026, tallying 35 saves with a 2.47 ERA in his age-30 season. He was nails after a rocky start, with a 1.30 ERA in his final 43 appearances. He's the top free-agent closer, and he's going to get paid. Blackburn won't be in Bednar's pay grade, but the former starter should have his list of suitors after shining out of the bullpen with a 1.69 ERA in 62 appearances. Blackburn, who was claimed off waivers from the Mets last season, joined a growing group of former starters the Yankees have taken from the scrap heap to convert into elite relievers.

They are two of the seven New York relievers going into free agency. The Yankees could re-sign any combination of the six -- Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Michael Fulmer and John Schreiber are the others -- but they'll likely turn to internal (and more affordable) options to fill out the group. That list includes prospect Carlos Lagrange and former AL Rookie of the Year winner Luis Gil, who was moved to the bullpen this season. If the Yankees don't trade from their rotation depth, they also could move one of Clarke Schmidt, Will Warren and Ryan Weathers to the bullpen.

Who replaces Chisholm and Grisham? Chisholm and Grisham were important contributors, but the Yankees have replacements ready. And both players will likely land multiyear contracts elsewhere -- assuming Chisholm declines the Yankees' qualifying offer, should they extend it. Anthony Volpe or Jose Caballero could replace Chisholm as the every-day second baseman. Spencer Jones could slide into Grisham's spot in center field. Or the Yankees make a splash for bigger upgrades at those spots.

Offseason prediction: A year after closer Devin Williams and setup man Luke Weaver left the Bronx for the Mets, the Yankees re-sign Bednar and Blackburn to stabilize the back end of their bullpen. A bonus prediction: They add a right-handed-hitting catcher to pair with Austin Wells via free agency or trade. Ryan Jeffers is the top free agent option. -- Castillo

Atlanta Braves
Eliminated by: Los Angeles Dodgers

Key free agents: RHP Tyler Mahle, RHP Raisel Iglesias, LHP Martin Perez, UT Mauricio Dubon, DH Dominic Smith

Biggest offseason priority: Shortstop. Ha-Seong Kim is also a free agent and he was a $20 million disaster, hitting .116 in 147 at-bats. Dubon ended up starting the most games there, 51, but he's also a free agent, and his best role is as a utility guy. Rookie Jim Jarvis started 35 games, but he hit .207 with one home run. Prospect Tate Southisene is a couple of years away.

Aside from that, re-signing Mahle, who pitched so well after coming over at the trade deadline, is another big priority given the uncertainty of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach returning from injuries. Didier Fuentes will be ready to replace Iglesias as closer, so given the subtraction of Kim, Fuentes and other free agents, there should be room to bring back Mahle.

Is it time to consider extensions for Ronald Acuna Jr. and Ozzie Albies? Remember those super team-friendly contracts signed years ago? They're getting close to the end. Acuna has two team options left, while Albies is entering the final year of his deal. The Braves will pick up the 2027 options -- $17 million for Acuna and $7 million for Albies -- but you wonder about the long-term futures in Atlanta for both players. Acuna didn't have a superstar season and got injured once again, playing 102 games. Albies played all 162 games but hit just .237/.293/.392. The easiest and perhaps wisest thing to do is just to let those contracts play out. Given his injury history, Acuna is going to be a risky bet in his 30s. Albies is entering his age-30 season, but that declining OBP is a problem. The Braves got unbelievable value out of those deals. No need to overpay now.

Offseason prediction: The shortstop free agent class is weak. (J.P. Crawford doesn't have much range and the others all played for the Braves -- Dubon, Kim and Jorge Mateo.) There could be a trade for somebody like Milwaukee's Joey Ortiz, who might be squeezed out of a crowded infield situation there, or taking on a potential salary dump like Boston's Trevor Story. (The Red Sox would have to eat most of his $25 million salary, plus he has declining range metrics as well.) So ... maybe bring back Dubon? Otherwise, the payroll situation dictates moving on from Iglesias, but Fuentes has the talent to be an elite closer. Mahle will be in demand, and maybe the likes of JR Ritchie and AJ Smith-Shawverr, plus Strider and Schwellenbach, will have the Braves feeling good enough about their rotation options. -- Schoenfield

San Diego Padres
Eliminated by: Milwaukee Brewers

Key free agents: RHP Michael King (player option), LHP Adrian Morejon, RHP Walker Buehler, 1B Ty France, LHP Robbie Ray, RHP Casey Mize

Biggest offseason priority: Nick Pivetta spent enough time on the injured list for his player option to turn into a club option, allowing the Padres to retain him for 2027. It's a boost for a team that will see a lot of starting pitchers depart via free agency this offseason, but more is needed. Assuming Pivetta is back, he'll be joining a rotation headlined by Yu Darvish and Joe Musgrove, two guys whose health will be a complete unknown going into next season. Outside of them, the Padres have Randy Vasquez and JP Sears as depth -- and little else.

How much will the new owners spend? Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones have said all the right things thus far, talking up their desire to win, complimenting late owner Peter Seidler's vision and speaking passionately about the Padres' importance to the community. We'll find out soon just how committed they are from a financial standpoint. The Padres have a lot of big contracts on their books -- for Manny Machado, Xander Bogaerts, Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. -- but also lots of holes that their depleted farm system can't fill. In order to continue to contend, they need to continue to spend. To what extent Feliciano and Jones do so remains to be seen. And before we learn that, we'll need to see what baseball's economic model looks like under a new collective bargaining agreement.

Offseason prediction: In the midst of a champagne celebration after clinching a third consecutive trip to the playoffs, Tatis stood by Morejon and clamored for general manager A.J. Preller to bring him back. "Pay him!" Tatis continually yelled toward Preller in Spanish. The guess here: The Padres find a way to bring Morejon back, pairing him with Mason Miller in the back end of their bullpen to continue to shut down games. Another guess: They also bring back France, who signed a minor league deal and performed like one of the game's best first basemen in 2026. The Padres need them both. -- Gonzalez

Teams eliminated in wild-card series

Boston Red Sox
Eliminated by: New York Yankees

Key free agents: RHP Sonny Gray ($30 million mutual option), LHP Patrick Sandoval, IF Isiah Kiner-Falefa

Biggest offseason priority: Gray had a terrific season but has hinted at retirement, telling The Boston Globe that he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family wants him home, so replacing him in the rotation could be the priority. A healthy Garrett Crochet will help fill that void, but after trading away so many starting pitchers and pitching prospects over the past year (including Kyle Harrison, Shane Drohan, Hunter Dobbins, Connelly Early, Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon), adding depth in that department looks necessary.

Will they trade Jarren Duran? While the Red Sox had a revolving door at shortstop and second base in 2026 -- six different players started at short and seven at second -- those positions will probably be resolved in 2027 with top prospect Franklin Arias and Curtis Mead, the trade deadline acquisition the Red Sox were going to play at second base until he got injured his first game with the team. Trevor Story still has one more year left on his contract, but there's no reason he should be playing ahead of Arias next season.

That leaves trading Duran on the agenda. Roman Anthony's nearly four-month stint on the IL meant the four-outfielders-for-three-positions problem never actually turned into a problem, but after hitting just .207/.266/.361, Duran is clearly fourth on the depth chart. His trade value took a nosedive, but he still somehow has two years left of team control, and the Red Sox will find a team willing to take a chance on him.

Offseason prediction: Even if there was no looming lockout, it would project as a quiet offseason for the Red Sox. The trades for Willson Contreras last offseason and then Mead, Adley Rutschman and reliever Erik Miller at the deadline brought in players with control through at least 2027. Maybe Duran gets traded, maybe it's time to give up on Tristan Casas ever getting healthy. If Gray returns -- $30 million is certainly a reason to stick around -- the Red Sox are in outstanding shape to return to the playoffs and make a run at the AL East title. -- Schoenfield

Chicago Cubs
Eliminated by: San Diego Padres

Key free agents: RHP Kevin Gausman, OF Ian Happ, OF Seiya Suzuki, LHP Shota Imanaga, LHP Matthew Boyd (mutual option), RHP Clay Holmes (player option), C Carson Kelly (mutual option)

Biggest offseason priority: The Cubs need to rebuild their pitching staff and that includes both their rotation and bullpen. The good news is they can concentrate on that part of their team because they have enough position players to fill the void left by Happ and Suzuki, who are both likely to leave the team via free agency. But what does that staff look like with Justin Steele and eventually Cade Horton returning from injury? Do Holmes and Boyd return? One but not the other? And what does one make of a bullpen that was inconsistent? It's a yearly debate under Jed Hoyer, who doesn't like to spend big money on closers. The Cubs have paid for that decision at times -- though in other moments they've developed some good relievers. Pitching is the key to their offseason, whether it comes from within or from outside the organization.

What will they do at catcher? Kelly has been nothing short of excellent over his two years in Chicago. He's great at calling a game. He's great at the ABS challenge system. And he has been more than a serviceable hitter. Plus, he's a leader and a glue guy in the clubhouse. Chicago has an up-and-coming catcher in Owen Ayers and still has Miguel Amaya under team control, and Kelly has a mutual option, so it'll be interesting how the team handles the position.

Offseason prediction: The Cubs probably will do what they usually do: spend some on their rotation, but not on the pen. They shelled out a few dollars for middle relievers in Phil Maton and Hunter Harvey last year and it didn't work out, so unless they have an appetite for a big-time closer -- they almost never do -- it feels as if they'll try to build their bullpen with minor additions and under-the-radar guys. Boyd might return, but Holmes, Imanaga and Gausman will test the market, opening up some slots in the rotation. -- Rogers

Houston Astros
Eliminated by: Chicago White Sox

Key free agents: RHP Bryan Abreu, 3B Isaac Paredes (club option, converted to mutual option if Paredes lands in top 10 of AL MVP balloting)

Biggest offseason priority: The Astros navigated the stretch run without a general manager after Dana Brown was let go in late August. That was after the draft and the trade deadline, so the committee guiding the front office was able to make it work. Going forward, the Astros will need to find or promote a new lead executive, then empower him to implement his own processes. Given the influence of owner Jim Crane and ex-player Jeff Bagwell, a vocal analytics skeptic in the past, the outcome of the search will tell us a lot about how the higher-ups in Houston see the landscape of best practices in the industry. That can be good, or not, but either way it's time the Astros returned some continuity to their most important baseball operations position.

How much weight should the Astros put on this playoff appearance? Of course the Astros deserved to celebrate the latest in the spree of division titles the franchise has won over the past decade. And it's certainly true that Houston's ability to climb out of a 20-31 hole in late May was fairly remarkable. Nevertheless, the Astros had to win their last two games to reach .500 at season's end and were outscored by 32 runs overall. If not for the low bar the AL West set this season, the Astros would have been watching from the playoff sideline for a second straight season. Thus, as the next Astros GM sets out, they'll have to be clear-eyed about it. The starting point for the club is one of mediocrity and there aren't enough upward-pointing trajectory arrows on the roster. Maybe a full reset isn't needed, but at the very least, the short and the long terms will have to be given equal shrift, or else this thing could really crumble in a hurry.

Offseason prediction: Houston has had a coterie of bright front office personalities working out of the spotlight going back to the Jeff Luhnow days. The most obvious course of action would be to promote one of them -- someone like assistant GMs Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey or Connor Huff. But just as crucial is to empower that hire to build and run their own front office. Questions about whether the Crane/Bagwell-led leadership team is willing to fully commit to that are why a promotion from within seems like the most likely course of action. The first indication about how this will go probably will be whether the Astros wait to have a new baseball chief in place before committing to bringing back manager Joe Espada in 2027. -- Doolittle

Philadelphia Phillies
Eliminated by: Atlanta Braves

Key free agents: 3B/1B Alec Bohm, 2B Luis Arraez, IF Edmundo Sosa, LHP Jose Alvarado, LHP Tim Mayza

Biggest offseason priority: Probably right field. But after yet another bullpen meltdown in the playoffs, Dave Dombrowski will once again look to reconfigure the relief corps. Don Mattingly made the right call in going to Jhoan Duran in the seventh inning of the Game 1 loss to the Braves, but the issue is the lack of depth that necessitated going to him so early.

The Adolis Garcia signing was a flop, so the Phillies eventually traded for Arraez and reconfigured their defense on the fly, shifting Bryson Stott to third base, Bohm to first base and Bryce Harper to right field. Harper presumably moves back to first base and Stott to second. Bohm is a goner, with top infield prospect Aidan Miller hopefully ready to take over third after missing almost all of 2026 because of a back injury. With the overall decline of the offense, that leaves a power-hitting right fielder -- good luck! -- as the biggest need.

Do the Phillies run it back with this same group ... again? There are worse places to start than a rotation with Cristopher Sanchez, Zack Wheeler and Jesus Luzardo, so there's no need to blow this up after another disappointing playoff exit. The position player core was not good in 2026, and Harper and Kyle Schwarber, the two mainstays who carried this group, aren't getting any younger, so this is an ever-growing concern. Check out the WAR of some of the other returning players: Trea Turner (-0.1), Justin Crawford (-0.2), All-Star Brandon Marsh (0.4), J.T. Realmuto (0.0). Bohm was below replacement as well. There isn't much immediate help on the farm either, other than Miller and pitcher Gage Wood.

Offseason prediction: No team in recent history has stuck with the same core group of players as long as the Phillies have. They will finally see some turnover with Bohm's departure, but there isn't a lot of room to maneuver here. This will be the team once again, with Dombrowski probably solving right field in the same way as 2026 -- signing a low-upside veteran -- and trying to improve the bullpen that had the worst ERA in the majors in September and was 21st for the season. -- Schoenfield
